title: Request guards checked before the body is parsed, the renderer that turns what an app raised into the envelope, and the workbook pairing with holy-sheet

functions.guard: guard({headers, body, limits?, config?}) -> {pass, requestId?} | {status, headers, body, bodyRead?}
functions.render: render({throw, config?, headers?}) -> {status, headers, body} | {passthrough, status}

contract.summary: Normative text: suites/http/SPEC.md sections 3 to 5. body is a string (sent as UTF-8), {hex}, or a file reference. "$generated" anywhere in an expected string stands for the generated request id: a lowercase UUID v4, the same in the header and the body. bodyRead is reported on body_too_large and bad_request refusals only: none = not one body byte requested; bounded = at most maxBodyBytes + 1 bytes plus one transport chunk. Expected headers are a subset, names lowercase.
contract.referenceNote: Authored from suites/http/SPEC.md in scripts/build-http-cases.py on 2026-11-12, before any implementation existed. The workbook rows' counts were measured by running fancy-holy-sheet 0.13.2 from the envelope's sibling checkout; everything else is typed from the spec. tests/http-probe.ts passes every row but the workbook ones, which need holy-sheet.

notes: The 413/400 rows marked bodyRead none are the reason this suite exists: refusing a body after reading it is what the guard is for avoiding.
PHP-FPM parses multipart and urlencoded bodies before any PHP runs, so those rows use other media types; the Laravel README states the post_max_size arrangement instead.
The workbook rows need holy-sheet in the runner's test environment (first-party). The probe does not run them.
